clue.text: Liberal repetition not on for well-educated types

indicators.note: 'not on' asks for the two letters of the word on to be dropped from the synonym

parts.note: an iteration is a repetition of a process
taken as written

explanation.surface: A liberal habit of repeating oneself is frowned upon among the educated classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes ON from ITERATION, leaving ITERATI.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are the learned, literary class of people, plural like the definition.

clue.text: Six-footer scoffing at little boy's conduct

indicators.note: scoffing means eating greedily, so the insect swallows the other pieces

parts.note: a bee is an insect, and every insect has six legs
taken as written
Tim is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: An insect is caught eating a small child's behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffing' reads as mocking, but here it means eating, so the insect swallows the other pieces; the 's is a link standing for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat time is to mark the rhythm for musicians, which is what a conductor does with a baton.

clue.text: Is empowered to reproduce the dance

indicators.note: to reproduce something is to make a second copy, so the word is written twice

parts.note: someone who can is able or permitted to act

explanation.surface: Someone has the authority to stage a performance of the dance again.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking dance from Parisian music halls.

clue.text: Fool kidnapping sailor, the bounder

indicators.note: kidnapping means holding someone captive, so the fool's letters surround the sailor

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a silly person
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: An idiot abducts a seaman, behaving like a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bounder' suggests a cad, but here it is literally something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallaby is a small kangaroo-like marsupial that moves by bounding.

clue.text: Commercial office almost silent, making further note

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a den is a private room or study

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: dumb means silent

explanation.surface: An advertising office falls nearly quiet, then produces another memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from DUMB, leaving DUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is a supplementary item added to a text, a note appended afterwards.

clue.text: Terribly erotic show, American for a change

definitions.note: the definition reads as 'an American word meaning a change'

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadfully racy performance prompts an American to switch channels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges EROTIC SHOW. The definition is not 'for a change' alone: the clue says the word is American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A switcheroo is US slang for a sudden reversal or swap, a surprising change.

clue.text: Partners inspiring only silly leggings

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the partners take the other letters inside

parts.note: North and South are partners at bridge

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of the word are put in a foolish order

explanation.surface: A couple encourage a single item of ridiculous legwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' scrambles the word only; 'inspiring' reads as encouraging, but here it means breathing in, so the bridge partners take that jumble inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings, coverings for the legs.

clue.text: Projection of American design

indicators.note: a design here is an arrangement, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film screening built to an American pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinerama was a widescreen film projection system using three projectors.

clue.text: Backward solver married an American philosopher

indicators.note: backward tells the solver to read the joined pieces from end to start

parts.note: ye is an old word for you, the person solving
wed means married

explanation.surface: A slow-witted puzzler weds a thinker from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns the whole of YEWED into DEWEY. 'Backward' looks like a description of a dim solver.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dewey was a pragmatist thinker from the United States, known for writings on education.

clue.text: Put to one side — this one?

definitions.text: Put to one side — this one?

parts.words: Put to one side — this one?
parts.note: something set aside has been abandoned, and the clue also asks which of the two sides it names

explanation.definitionFit: Left means abandoned or set aside, and it also names one of the two sides.

clue.text: Pass old reading pile

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a lection is an old word for a reading, especially from scripture

explanation.surface: Get through an old book from a stack.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection is a gathered heap or accumulation of things, like a pile.

clue.text: Continues to obstruct fruit

parts.note: to dam a flow is to obstruct it
on means continuing, as in carry on, so 'dams on' is to continue obstructing

explanation.surface: Something keeps blocking the passage of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continues to obstruct' reads as 'dams on', keeps damming; the clue gives the idea before the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark purple plum, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: London borough (West) cuts instrument for joiner

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so these pieces go inside the instrument

parts.note: the sax is a musical instrument
Ealing is a borough of west London

explanation.surface: A west London borough slashes the instrument budget for a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' means slices into the instrument; 'joiner' suggests a carpenter but describes something that fastens.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealing wax is used to fasten envelopes and documents shut, so it joins things together.

clue.text: Zola has corrupted this spiritual type

parts.note: Zola Budd was a South African-born runner who competed for Britain

indicators.note: corrupted means spoilt or altered, so the word's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The novelist Zola has spoilt this mystic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zola' points to the writer Emile Zola, but it is the athlete's first name. 'corrupted' rearranges THIS to HIST; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Buddhist follows the religious teachings of the Buddha, a person of spiritual practice.

clue.text: Inland Revenue in error, one's far from short!

indicators.note: in places the tax office's letters within the blunder

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder
IR stands for Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: The tax office has blundered, but nobody's short-changed.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is the tallest living animal, so a creature that is anything but small.

clue.text: Starter in pastry dish, hot item

indicators.note: in places the beginner within the pastry dish

parts.note: a flan is an open pastry case with a filling
a tiro is a beginner or novice

explanation.surface: A first course in a pastry dish, served hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a menu course; it is a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron was a heavy iron heated on a stove for pressing clothes.

clue.text: Having lost head, individual rings me, an American philosopher

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the shortened word surrounds the other piece
losing its head means the first letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a person is an individual
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beheaded individual telephones me, an American thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having lost head' beheads the individual; 'rings' suggests telephoning but means encircling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American essayist and the leading transcendentalist thinker.

clue.text: On film, torment predictable

parts.note: taken as written
ET is the Spielberg film about an alien
to rack is to torture or torment

explanation.surface: A film shown on screen is a torment of obvious plotting.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-track mind thinks only about one thing, so it is narrow and easy to foresee.

clue.text: For each dynastic name, half remains, possibly

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour

indicators.note: half means only the first four of the eight letters are kept

parts.note: Hapsburg is the name of the European royal dynasty

explanation.surface: For each royal house, only half of its legacy survives, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps HAPS from HAPSBURG; 'remains' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and possibly are synonyms, both meaning maybe.

clue.text: I'm dividing all that's 10, the rough value

indicators.note: dividing means splitting apart, so these letters split the other word

parts.note: 10 points to the answer at 10-across; an estate is everything a person leaves when they die
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: I'm sharing out what remains, giving an approximate worth.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' stands for the answer to 10-across, so 'all that's 10' is what a dead person leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate calculation of a value or amount.

clue.text: Brief novel penned by fifth columnist

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the novel sits inside the spy

parts.note: a fifth columnist is a traitor working inside, a spy
Kim is a novel by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: A short novel written by a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' suggests writing, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy means scanty or short, as with brief clothing.

clue.text: Prison now with air conditioning?

definitions.meaning: a building with air conditioning is chillier than before

explanation.definitionFit: Cooler is slang for a jail and also means less warm.

clue.text: Swimmer holds up an American philosopher

indicators.note: holds means the fish surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a carp is a fish, a swimmer

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A fish props up a thinker from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the little word, and 'holds' puts it inside the fish. 'an' is fodder here, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Carnap was a German-born logical positivist who worked in the United States.

clue.text: Man approaching shipping forecast area sees bird

parts.note: a king is a chess piece, one of the men
Fisher is one of the sea areas in the BBC radio shipping forecast

explanation.surface: A man nearing a North Sea weather zone spots a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The shipping forecast is a BBC radio sea-weather bulletin naming areas around Britain; 'approaching' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingfisher is a brightly coloured bird that dives for fish.

clue.text: An easy dessert?

parts.note: reads as a simple pudding, but easy also describes a promiscuous person

explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a pastry dessert and also slang for a promiscuous woman.

clue.text: See 2
Children manipulate this, said an American philosopher

indicators.note: an American accent softens the t, so the name is spoken like the modelling clay

parts.note: Play-Doh is a modelling clay children knead

explanation.surface: An American says children play with this, as a thinker once put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an American philosopher' looks like the definition, as in other clues here; the philosopher is Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Socrates.

clue.text: Source of drugs full of speed to contain injury

indicators.note: to contain means the fast word encloses the injury

parts.note: pacy means fast
harm is injury

explanation.surface: A fast-acting drug supply that also causes damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is a shop dispensing medicines.
